World of Warcraft: Forever is included with an active World of Warcraft subscription or Game Time.
You play on Windows or Mac with keyboard and mouse; controller support is available in beta.
In Europe, servers open on November 5, 2026 at 12:00 a.m. CET, which is November 4 at 23:00 UTC.

Sign up from the Battle.net Login page, or open the Battle.net Shop and select Account > Create Account. Verify your email, choose a secure password and consider enabling two-factor authentication. If you already have an account, this wiki’s “Installing the game and recovering your account” page (link at the bottom) explains how to get back into it.
Forever needs no separate purchase: it is included with an active World of Warcraft subscription or Game Time. Only the new Skyborne race requires the Heroic Pack or a higher digital upgrade.
Download the Battle.net desktop app, sign in, install World of Warcraft and select World of Warcraft: Forever from the available game versions.
The game runs on Windows and Mac with keyboard and mouse. Controller support is available in a beta state for players who prefer a gamepad. Before installing, review the current system requirements.

There is also a graphics card floor: Forever needs a GPU based on one of these microarchitectures or newer: AMD Graphics Core Next 1 (2012), NVIDIA Maxwell (2014) or Intel Skylake (2015). Blizzard ties it to the game’s new visual look and notes that most players already use compatible hardware.
Compatible examples given by Blizzard: AMD Radeon HD 7850, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 9xx and 750/750 Ti, Intel HD Graphics 530; these cards are still well below the game’s minimum requirements.
Unsupported examples: AMD Radeon HD 6950, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 760/770/780 and GTX 8xxM, Intel HD Graphics 6000.
To check your card on Windows: Settings > System > Display > Advanced display, or Device Manager under Display adapters.
Upgrade editions are optional and sold on the Battle.net Shop; for the game itself, only the Skyborne race depends on them.

Skyborne Heroic Pack: the Skyborne race and their Zephras Isle starting quests, Early Name Reservation, the Cerulean Prideclaw mount (you buy the riding skill in game to use it), cosmetics, housing decor and one Invite-A-Friend Launch Code.

Skyborne Epic Pack: everything in the Heroic Pack, plus 30 days of Game Time starting at launch, more cosmetics, pets, tabards and three Invite-A-Friend Launch Codes in total; it also gave access to the beta that opened on September 17.

Warcraft Forever Collection (limited time): everything in the Epic Pack, plus Warcraft III: Reforged, the Warcraft III Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom campaign and figurine decor for Housing in modern World of Warcraft.
Faction sets your starting communities, cities and stories; race sets your appearance, starting location and racial abilities; class sets how you play.
Nine races and nine classes are available, with new combinations such as Orc Mages or Dwarf Shamans.
Your name has two parts, and the full combination must be unique within your region.

Your faction, Alliance or Horde, determines which communities, cities and stories your character begins with. Your race determines your appearance, starting location and racial abilities. Your class determines how you play: up close, at range, casting spells, protecting a group, healing allies or combining several roles.

The nine classes are Druid, Hunter, Mage, Paladin, Priest, Rogue, Shaman, Warlock and Warrior. Blizzard advises considering both the class you want to play and the races that can become it; the full table is on the wiki’s “Races and classes: every combination” page (link at the bottom).
Forever opens new combinations: Orc Mages, Troll Warlocks, Undead Paladins, Human Hunters, Gnome Priests and Dwarf Shamans.

The Alliance brings together Humans, Dwarves, Gnomes and Night Elves; the Horde, Orcs, Undead, Tauren and Trolls; the Skyborne can join either. Each race’s history is told in this guide’s three “Race history” pages: the Alliance, the Horde and the Skyborne.

In Forever, racial abilities have been reworked to be stronger and more distinct: each race has two active and two passive abilities, tuned to offer similar offensive power while keeping their own utility. Blizzard has detailed a few examples.

Dwarves: Stoneform still removes Bleeds, Poisons and Diseases and grants immunity to them, but its defensive bonus now reduces Physical damage taken instead of increasing Armor; Find Treasure can stay active alongside other tracking, Mace Specialization increases critical strike chance with all spells and abilities while using a mace, and Big Game Hunter increases damage against Beasts.

Undead: Will of the Forsaken still removes Charm, Fear and Sleep but no longer grants immunity to them; Cannibalize also restores Mana; Underwater Breathing is unchanged; the new Touch of the Grave gives attacks a chance to drain life from enemies.

Skyborne, both paths: Walk on Air (glide for 10 seconds), Wind Blessed (passive, 1% Haste) and Elemental Insight (passive, 5% more damage to Elementals); Windshapers (Horde) add Skysight (10% run speed), the High Order (Alliance) Read Ley Line (100% increased Health and Mana regeneration).

At character creation, you choose whether your Skyborne joins the Horde (elemental traditions, access to the Shaman class) or the Alliance (arcane legacy, access to the Mage class). Both begin on Zephras Isle, a level 1–12 starting zone. Skyborne access requires the Heroic Pack or higher digital upgrades.
Both paths can also become Warriors, Hunters, Rogues or Druids, with druid forms made for the Skyborne.

For each new character, you choose High Definition models and animations (more detailed) or Standard Definition (the original World of Warcraft look). This choice affects appearance only, not abilities or progression, and can be changed later in the Options or at a Barbershop in game.

Each character has a main name and a secondary name, like a first name and a surname. Two characters can share a first name as long as their full names differ: the full combination must be unique within the region.
To hide your secondary name in the world: Escape > Options > Nameplates, then check “My Secondary Name”. It still appears in chat.

Names must follow the in-game code of conduct. The system evaluates both parts together, so splitting a restricted word across the two names will not necessarily work. No name is guaranteed; if yours is taken, choose another combination or try the random name generator. Early Name Reservation is covered on the wiki’s “Getting ready for launch” page (link at the bottom).
The preset does not lock you in: each setting can be changed under Game Menu > Options, and the choice screen only appears at your first login.
The ruleset sets how PvP works and which community conventions apply; if unsure, the official guide suggests Normal.
Groups, guilds, dungeons and raids only work with the same ruleset and faction: agree with friends before creating your characters.

Classic offers a presentation closer to the original game, with simpler visuals and less automatic guidance; Enhanced offers higher visual fidelity and more interface features enabled by default. If you are unsure, the official guide suggests Enhanced. Each preset’s starting settings are listed on the “Choosing a preset: Classic or Enhanced” page (link at the bottom).
Normal: adventuring and fighting monsters, with PvP at your discretion.
PvP: opposing players can attack you in the open world.
Roleplay and Roleplay-PvP: stricter naming and behavior rules for playing in character; the PvP version adds the risk of being attacked.
Hardcore: announced for later, where a character’s death is final.
The full ruleset comparison is on the wiki’s “Choosing a ruleset” page (link at the bottom).

You cannot group across rulesets, and Horde and Alliance cannot group together; only battlegrounds may mix players from several rulesets, except Hardcore. To play under another ruleset, you create a new character there. The “Choose where to play with friends” page (link at the bottom) covers these cases.
On the PvP ruleset you can only create characters for one faction; on Normal, Roleplay and Hardcore, both factions are possible.

To meet players who share your language, open the Game Menu (Escape) > Options > Languages and Social (under System), then pick your “Preferred Online Language”. The setting is account-wide and can only be changed once every 24 hours.
Characters with a quest to share have an exclamation point above their heads; a question mark means a completed quest is ready to turn in.
The Quest Log (L key), the world map (M key) and the Spellbook (P key) are the three windows to learn first.
After dying, you come back to life by returning to your body from the graveyard; the Spirit Healer lets you resurrect on the spot, but damages your gear and may weaken your character for a while.

An accepted quest is added to the Quest Log and its objectives show automatically on screen. When there are too many, not all of them appear: the L key opens the full Quest Log, where you can read each quest’s story and objectives, track or untrack it, and abandon one if the log is full.
The M key opens the world map with quest markers and highlighted objective areas; the minimap also points toward nearby objectives.
The guide advises reading quest text, which tells the story of the area and often gives clues, and taking your time while watching the level of nearby enemies when you leave the road.

The Escape key opens the Game Menu; Options lets you adjust controls and key bindings, action bars, nameplates, chat, audio, graphics and accessibility. The guide recommends starting with the default settings.
Newly learned spells are no longer added to your action bars automatically: drag them from the Spellbook.
Your action bar holds the abilities you use in battle; place the most useful ones within easy reach and read their tooltips.
The P key opens the Spellbook: drag an ability onto the action bar, and change its key binding under Game Menu > Options > Keybindings.
As you gain levels, visit your class trainer to learn new abilities.
Watch your health and resources and carry food and drink: innkeepers sell them and can bind your Hearthstone to their inn.
While learning, pull one enemy at a time.
At launch, creatures respawn faster in low-level zones, especially starting zones; Blizzard will bring these timers back to normal once the rush is over.

After death, releasing your spirit brings you back at a nearby graveyard. The minimap corpse marker, or the world map (M key), shows where your body is; once close enough, select Resurrect, ideally somewhere safe.

You can also speak with the Spirit Healer at the graveyard to resurrect there: this damages your equipment’s durability and may apply Resurrection Sickness, which greatly reduces your effectiveness. The guide then advises avoiding combat until it expires and repairing your gear as soon as you can.
The official guide says controller support is available in a beta state for players who prefer a gamepad; keyboard and mouse remain the way of playing described everywhere else in this guide.

During the Forever beta, the official development notes described a “Gamepad (Alpha)” section in the game options, with for example a compact action bar and fixed party targeting on the directional pad. These options may still change: check them in the Options menu once in game.
November 4, 2026: added changes from the November 2 development notes (spells no longer auto-added to bars, faster respawns).
Hover over an item to compare it with what you wear: a higher-quality item is not always the best choice for your class.
Items with gray names have no further use and can be safely sold.
Each character can learn two primary professions and all three secondary professions.

Hover over an item in your bags to read its tooltip: when it can replace equipped gear, both items are shown (armor, damage, attributes, level requirements, other effects). Also check armor type, weapon compatibility and the attributes useful to your class.
To equip an item, right-click it in your bags or drag it onto the matching slot in the Character panel; the C key opens that panel.
Right-click a merchant to open the shop, then right-click one of its items to buy it, or an item in your bags to sell it.
Sold something by mistake? Check the Buyback tab before leaving.
Vendors with an anvil icon repair damaged equipment for a fee.
Training every class ability from 1 to 60 costs between 206 and 207 gold, whatever the class.
Bags fill quickly: sell what you no longer need in town and store materials you want to keep in a bank. If unsure about an item, start by reading its tooltip.
Bags no longer equip themselves into a free slot: equip them yourself.
Gathering: Herbalism (herbs), Mining (ore and stone), Skinning (leather and hides).
Crafting: Alchemy (potions), Blacksmithing (weapons and armor), Enchanting (gear enhancements), Engineering (gadgets), Leatherworking (leather and mail armor), Tailoring (cloth gear and bags).
Secondary: Cooking (food), Fishing (ingredients), First Aid (survival supplies).
Cooking has an extra role in Forever: its basic campfire creates a shared campsite where players can rest and craft together to earn beneficial effects. Guide 6/6 explains how to use it.

To learn or advance a profession, speak with its trainer in a starting area or major city; if you cannot find one, ask a city guard and follow the marker on your map. The K key opens the Professions interface: learned professions, skill levels, recipes and required materials.

Groups, guilds, dungeons and raids only work with players on the same ruleset and faction.
A dungeon group is generally five players: a tank, a healer and damage dealers.
The WoW Portal Room is the official World of Warcraft Discord server.

Invite nearby players, join a guild or ask for help in chat. Note that you can only group with characters on the same ruleset and faction; the “Choose where to play with friends” page (link at the bottom) covers this.
To communicate without words, type an emote in chat, such as /wave, /cheer, /dance or /thank, then press Enter; /emote followed by an action creates a custom emote.

Dungeons are instanced adventures filled with enemies, bosses and valuable rewards. The tank draws enemy attention, the healer keeps the party standing and damage dealers (DPS) defeat the creatures. The official guide asks for patience with yourself and others.

Forever adds nine new five-player dungeons, levels 13 to 60. The first are the Hall of Thanes (levels 13–18, beneath Ironforge, Dun Morogh) and the Ruins of Lordaeron (levels 15–20, above the Undercity, Tirisfal Glades); each has its own wiki page.

Early on, a short quest introduces the Camping system: Cooking’s Basic Campfire creates a shared campsite where anyone can rest. Up to three profession-made items can be added, one per player; sit or craft there for at least 1 minute to gain their benefits.
Choose your spot carefully: danger can find you when you stop, more so on a PvP ruleset. The full item-by-item system is on the wiki’s “Camping and crafting” page (link at the bottom).

The WoW Portal Room brings together players and WoW Ambassadors, experienced players who represent their Discord communities and help everyone find a space that suits them. Like any portal, it is a gateway, not the final destination.
The Alliance has four original races: Humans, Dwarves, Gnomes and Night Elves; High Order Skyborne can also join it (see the Skyborne page).
Stormwind is described as the backbone of the Alliance; Dwarves and Gnomes come from Khaz Modan; the Night Elves’ capital, Darnassus, lies in the World Tree Teldrassil.
Gnomeregan, the gnomes’ city, is lost at the time of Forever.

According to Blizzard, the noble races of the Alliance are bound together by proud traditions of nobility, honor, faith, justice and sacrifice, and contribute their technical, arcane and spiritual wisdom toward a peaceful and just world.

Humans are a young and highly versatile race, mastering combat, craftsmanship and magic with stunning efficiency. Their valor and optimism led them to build some of the world’s greatest kingdoms. In this troubled era, after generations of conflict, humanity seeks to rekindle its former glory.

Their capital is Stormwind. The human kingdom of Stormwind forms the backbone of the Alliance; its strength is its willingness to seek diplomatic solutions, and its citizens defend their home by the principles of honor and justice. The city’s monuments honor the sacrifices of past heroes.

Dwarves are an ancient race descended from the earthen, titan-forged beings of living stone created when the world was young. Hailing from Ironforge in the snowy peaks of Khaz Modan, they are courageous defenders of the Alliance. Their capital, Ironforge, is carved into the mountain around a massive forge.

For ages, dwarves cared only for riches from the earth’s depths. Then records surfaced of a god-like race said to have given them life and an enchanted birthright. Since then they have pursued lost artifacts and ancient knowledge, and dwarven archaeologists are scattered throughout the globe.

Though small in stature, the gnomes of Khaz Modan used their great intellect to secure a place in history. Their subterranean kingdom, Gnomeregan, was once a marvel of steam-driven technology, but the city was lost to a massive trogg invasion. Its builders are now vagabonds in the dwarven lands, aiding their allies as best they can.

The official race page highlights their optimism in the face of calamity, their boundless creativity and their commitment to the Alliance’s cause; Gnomeregan was their capital until that trogg invasion.

Ten thousand years ago, the night elves founded a vast empire, but their reckless use of magic brought them to ruin. In grief, they withdrew to the forests and remained isolated until the return of their ancient enemy, the Burning Legion; with no other choice, they emerged to fight for their place in the new world.

Also known as the kaldorei, many still remember the War of the Ancients over ten thousand years ago, when they halted the Burning Legion’s first invasion of Azeroth. Their capital, Darnassus, lies in the boughs of Teldrassil, a massive World Tree, and reflects their reverence for nature.
The Horde has four original races: Orcs, Undead, Tauren and Trolls; Windshaper Skyborne can also join it (see the Skyborne page).
Tauren and Trolls joined the Horde through the orcs: a blood-debt for the former, friendship with Thrall for the latter.
The Forsaken, led by Sylvanas, see the Horde as merely a tool.

The proud nations of the Horde are loosely joined in an alliance of convenience against a hostile world that would see them destroyed. The Horde values strength and honor but struggles to keep aggression in check; it fights to build a world where its people can live free.

The orcs originated on another world, Draenor. A peaceful people with shamanic beliefs, they were enslaved by the Burning Legion and forced into war with the humans of Azeroth. It took many years, but they escaped the demons’ corruption and won their freedom; they still fight for honor in an alien world that reviles them.

The official race page adds that they were corrupted by Kil’jaeden, a demon lord of the Burning Legion. Once free, the orcs settled on Kalimdor, in Durotar, where they built their capital, Orgrimmar, named for the former Horde warchief Orgrim Doomhammer.

Death offered no escape for the humans killed during the Lich King’s campaign in Lordaeron. When his grasp over the Scourge faltered after the Third War, a group of undead broke free of his will: they call themselves the Forsaken. Their capital is the Undercity, a maze of catacombs, crypts and toxic sludge.

Led by the banshee Sylvanas, the Forsaken seek to overthrow the Lich King and take vengeance on the Scourge. Humans, bent on purging all undead from the land, are their enemies too. They care little for their allies: to them the Horde is merely a tool for their dark schemes.

The peaceful tauren, the shu’halo in their own tongue, have long dwelled in Kalimdor, striving to preserve the balance of nature for their goddess, the Earth Mother. Once nomadic, their tribes united and settled in their ancestral homeland of Mulgore. Their capital, Thunder Bluff, was founded by chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof and his tribe atop windswept mesas.

Recently attacked by murderous centaur, the tauren would have been wiped out but for a chance encounter with the orcs, who helped defeat the attackers. To honor this blood-debt, the tauren joined the Horde, sealing the two races’ friendship.

Once at home in the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale, the fierce trolls of the Darkspear tribe were pushed out by warring factions. They befriended the Horde, and Thrall, the orcs’ young warchief, convinced them to travel with him to Kalimdor. Though they cling to their shadowy heritage, they hold a place of honor in the Horde.

The official race page says these exiles were on the brink of extinction when a violent storm drove Thrall and his forces to their remote island; they were welcomed into the Horde among other outcast races. Since arriving on the Echo Isles long ago, they have been enthralled by Kalimdor’s raptors.
Two paths, one ancestry: the Windshapers (Horde) embrace elemental traditions, the High Order (Alliance) pursues the arcane legacy of their ancestors.
Classes: Druid, Hunter, Rogue and Warrior for both; Shaman for Windshapers, Mage for the High Order.
Access to the Skyborne and their starting zone requires the Heroic Pack or higher.

Thousands of years ago, a group of Highborne exiles forged a pact with elemental wind spirits and built a civilization within Skywall, one of the elemental planes. When you arrive on Zephras Isle, that civilization is in crisis: the air spirits that protected the island have vanished, ancient structures are failing, communities are becoming isolated and the people are divided over what comes next.

The Windshapers (Horde) descend from the first shen’dorei high elves to receive the wind spirits’ gift of elemental skysight. A new generation leaves Skywall for Azeroth to learn what became of their elemental mentors and restore the wind spirits. They can become Shaman.

The High Order (Alliance) is made up of descendants of the Highborne scholars of Eldre’Thalas. When the spirits vanished, it realized that the Skyborne’s dependence on their elemental patrons left them vulnerable; its new generation returns to Azeroth to reclaim lost arcane knowledge so the shen’dorei can survive on their own. They can become Mages.

Targeting allies and enemies, looting and menus are supported.
Settings are in Edit Mode and the Options menu.

Settings (Gamepad settings): Camera, HUD Modifier, Frame Focus Style, Action Bars, Targeting, Raid Targeting Options. On controllers with supported lighting, the light is red for a Horde character and blue for an Alliance character.

Ground-targeted items can be placed from the gamepad action bar (press again to confirm).
Ruleset selection screens, cinematic skipping, early exit from a flight (you land at the next flight point).
Focus target: LB + RB + bottom button.
Targeting friendly corpses and critters; enemy players can no longer be selected by friendly analog targeting.
Pet movement command; reworked bag interface (free space, ammo, keyring).
Each character has a first name and a secondary name. Two characters can share a first name as long as their full names differ; uniqueness applies across the region, not a realm.
The secondary name can suggest a family, a place or a reputation; Blizzard’s example is Asha, Thalen and Mira Brightvale (Clairvallon in French). A guild can also adopt a shared theme.
To hide your secondary name in the world: Escape > Options > Nameplates, then tick “My Secondary Name”; it still appears in chat.
Names must follow the in-game code of conduct.
Some words, spellings or repeated characters may be restricted, including names impersonating Blizzard.
Both parts are evaluated together: splitting a restricted word across them will not necessarily work.

You can group, run dungeons and raid with players on the same ruleset. Cross-ruleset grouping is not supported; battlegrounds may include players from other rulesets, except Hardcore, which stays separate.

This is not one giant realm: each ruleset is its own large ecosystem, designed so you keep crossing paths with familiar names.
You cannot freely hop between rulesets; to play elsewhere you create a new character. In Hardcore, a character that dies can transfer to another ruleset, including PvP.
Collections and Legacy Points are account-wide. The exception: Hardcore progress can carry elsewhere, but progress from other rulesets does not flow back into Hardcore.
On the PvP ruleset an account can only create characters of one faction; Normal, Roleplaying and Hardcore allow both.
To keep Horde and Alliance populations closer, Blizzard plans tools similar to Season of Discovery, where new character creation could be temporarily limited for a faction.

Over the previous weekend, a large group of non-elite enemies in Blackmaw Hold was wrongly dropping the full loot expected from an elite.
The bug was hotfixed early on November 16, according to the post published on the 17th.
Players who just ran the dungeon a few times and benefited without meaning to did nothing wrong and are not at risk.

A couple hundred players worldwide farmed that group exclusively knowing it was unintended: their accounts were economy-locked, the gold involved is being removed and significant abusers are suspended.

Blizzard says it is monitoring the game economy as players reach higher-level content. Finding efficient farming spots has been part of the game since 2004, but when a single location becomes so lucrative that it overshadows every other source, the team generally adjusts it to bring it in line.

On November 16, an economy lock was placed on the accounts involved to limit the impact while the extent of the gains was investigated, including gold earned by selling the bugged drops to vendors. On the 17th, Blizzard said it was removing that gold and applying account suspensions to significant abusers.
The post gives no suspension length, no amounts removed and no account names.

A player who ran Blackmaw Hold normally has nothing to fear for their account. However, Blizzard repeats that players should not abuse clearly unintended mechanics and that it will keep acting against intentional abuse.

Blizzard says beta changes, alongside Elemental adjustments, pushed Enhancement toward Intellect and spell-power gear and away from Windfury, which the team wants to keep at the heart of the specialization.
